## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `70b3cb0927cd817a09c947928dc33ed222e28e8e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/suggested-audience-bindings.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts + packages/spec/src/security/tenancy-posture.ts (postureEnforcesWall, normalizeTenancyPosture), packages/spec/src/security/high-privilege.ts (describeAnchorForbiddenBits, describeHighPrivilegeBits), packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts (the reader's packageId and disabled-package rule), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/builtin-positions.ts (declareEveryoneBaseline), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/app-default-permission-set.ts (appSecurityPluginOptions), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/suggested-audience-bindings.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/walled-accepted-defaults.boot.test.ts, .changeset/23385-walled-accepted-defaults.md, docs/adr/0131 (D3, D5, D7, D11, section 1.5), docs/adr/0090 (D5, D7, Alternatives 3)

Inputs: card #23385 (body and all seven comments, the ruling as triage quoted and verified it in 6205580248), this PR's body, file list and net diff against `main` at this head (six files, +582/-43; the three-dot and two-dot diffs of those paths against current `main` are identical, and no commit on `main` since the merge-base 34b740f2d touches plugin-security, ADR-0131, tenancy-posture, high-privilege or the security catalog), and the 40 check-runs on this head. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`SecurityPluginOptions.acceptedDefaultPermissionSets?: readonly string[]`** — a new optional member of the options interface reached through the package entry by `SecurityPlugin`'s constructor: a widening. RIGHT. Read once at construction by `readAcceptedDefaultPermissionSetsOption`: `undefined` is undeclared; a list of non-empty strings is deduplicated and frozen; anything else (`null`, a bare string, an empty or non-string entry) is a `TypeError` at construction, never read as "nothing accepted". RIGHT. Nit, not a defect: names are not trimmed, so a padded name is later withheld as unserved — loud, not silent.

2. **Read only under the walled posture.** `hostDeclaredAcceptance` returns the list only when `deployment.posture` is set and `postureEnforcesWall(posture)` holds (`posture !== 'single'`, tenancy-posture.ts). The posture is the plugin's one resolution in `start()` (`tenancy` service through `normalizeTenancyPosture`, else the `org-scoping` probe, else `single`), handed on through `deploymentAcceptance()` and `SuggestionDeps.posture()`; no second reading. RIGHT. **A declaration under `single` is refused at `start()`**, directly after that resolution, by `refuseAcceptedDefaultsWithoutWall`: the plugin's start throws and the kernel rolls back (boot pin: "failed to start - rollback complete"). RIGHT. Limit, stated not failed: `start()`'s two degraded early returns (no ObjectQL or metadata service; an engine without middleware) sit above the refusal, so on such a boot a declaration is neither read nor refused — that boot already warns that security middleware is not registered, and nothing derives `everyone` from the option there.

3. **The grant path, traced on every derivation.** `readAcceptedEveryoneSets(ql, metadata, deployment)`: declared, the candidates are the declared names and the record is not read; otherwise the pre-existing row path (Default Organization, `confirmed`, `deployment_decision`). Each candidate then passes the same four checks a row passes, in order: the catalog serves the name (`securityCatalogReaderOf(ql).resolve('permission', set)`, which does not serve a disabled package's item); the serving entry names a package (`entry.packageId`, the binding's `_packageId` — for a row it must equal the accepting package, for a declared name it must exist, ADR-0086 D3); `isDefault: true`; and `describeAnchorForbiddenBits(definition, 'everyone', capabilities)` (ADR-0090 D7: a system permission not excused by a declared capability, View or Modify All, delete or transfer, export). A failing name is withheld with its reason and never granted, `forbidden: true` for the D7 case. `declareEveryone` runs at `kernel:ready`, on every landed `permission` mutation, on package-uninstall cleanup and from the doors' `rederiveEveryone`, so a catalog change after boot (a set gains a forbidden bit, loses `isDefault`, its package is disabled or uninstalled) drops the grant at the next derivation, exactly as for an accepted row. RIGHT. Answer to the gate question: no declared value can put a high-privilege set, an unserved set, a package-less set or a non-`isDefault` set on `everyone`; `[]` grants nothing beyond the baseline, and an empty array is "declared" on every branch (sync, reconcile, derivation, all three doors — each checked).

4. **Withheld and logged at `error`, not refused at boot.** Judged RIGHT under "declared means enforced". The direction is fail-closed: the gate refuses the grant, and what goes unenforced is only the host's over-claim, which `declareEveryone` reports on every derivation — `error` for a forbidden bit, `warn` for the three other reasons — naming the set, the reason and the remedy (remove the name, or serve the set again as some package's `isDefault` set). That is the level AGENTS.md's degradation rule assigns to "looks normal while a claim did not land". Refusing the boot instead would make a post-boot package change a boot-breaker and would refuse a name whose package is not installed yet; the row path chose withhold-and-report for the same reasons, and the two paths now behave alike. The path a misconfigured host takes: construction accepts well-formed names; boot proceeds; `everyone` is the baseline plus the names that pass; every failing name is reported at every derivation; the three doors answer 409 naming the option; nothing silently grants. What the option lacks relative to the accept door is an acceptance-time 403 for a forbidden set; the `error` line on every derivation is the substitute, and the module pin and the boot pin cover it.

5. **The sync and the reconcile.** `syncAudienceBindingSuggestions` returns zero before any read or write when declared; `reconcileAudienceBindingSuggestions` skips the owner read, counts every existing row as not read and warns once per pass naming the option (rows kept, never deleted); the plugin's two `(non-fatal)` warn sites stay silent because nothing throws. RIGHT. Side effect recorded under ③: the early return is above `collectDeclaredSuggestions`, whose once-per-engine dropped-manifest-permissions report therefore does not run on a declared wall.

6. **The doors.** List, accept and dismiss all check the deployment authority first (a non-operator under a wall is 403, unchanged) and then refuse with 409 `SUGGESTION_STATE` and `hostDeclaredMessage` when declared (`requireRecordOwner` for accept and dismiss, an explicit check in list). Consistent. RIGHT. **Walled and undeclared** with no organization to own the record: list throws `noRecordOwnerMessage` from the sync when a package declares any `isDefault` set, as today; accept and dismiss answer 409 with the same text; the boot reconcile's `(non-fatal)` warn carries it. Behaviour unchanged, message new: it names the option, ADR-0131 D5 and section 1.5, says "an empty list when none is accepted", and no longer says "create the Default Organization". RIGHT. The one-organization-no-`default` case is unchanged in both arms, as the PR's table states. Carried-over wording nit: "there is more than one organization" is also what a deployment with zero organizations is told (`resolveDefaultOrganizationId` answers `undefined` for both); the old message said the same.

7. **`single` is byte-for-byte unchanged.** `NO_RECORD_OWNER_MESSAGE` is untouched (context lines in the diff); `noRecordOwnerMessage` returns it under `single` and under a missing posture; `hostDeclaredAcceptance` returns `undefined` there; the record path inside `readAcceptedEveryoneSets` is a refactor into `candidates` whose four checks, reason strings and `packageId` are the same as before, plus the new `source: 'record'`. The pre-existing tests in `suggested-audience-bindings.test.ts` are byte-unchanged (the diff adds three import names and one appended block) and green on this head. RIGHT.

8. **Exported widening.** A trailing optional `deployment?: DeploymentAcceptance` on `readAcceptedEveryoneSets`, `syncAudienceBindingSuggestions` and `reconcileAudienceBindingSuggestions` — additive; every pre-existing caller (the plugin's four sites and two tests inside the package; none outside the package on `main`, none in objectui) still compiles and reads the record. `SuggestionDeps.acceptedDefaultPermissionSets?` — additive. `DeploymentAcceptance` newly re-exported from `index.ts` — needed, since the public option and the widened signatures name it. `readAcceptedDefaultPermissionSetsOption` and `refuseAcceptedDefaultsWithoutWall` are module exports not re-exported from `index.ts`: package-internal, not on the published surface. All RIGHT for `Clause-②: yes (widening)`.

9. **`WithheldAcceptance.source: 'record' | 'host-configuration'` as a REQUIRED field.** The type is the output of `readAcceptedEveryoneSets` and is accepted as input by no exported function, so the package's accept set narrows nowhere; readers gain a field the producer always sets. Constructors: on `main` the only one is the producer's own `withheld.push` (repo-wide read; `metadata-core`'s `withheld.push(name)` is another type), and objectui has none; an out-of-tree test double would need the new field — the only sense in which this could be called a narrowing, and not an accept-set one. RIGHT as required; optional would make every reader handle `undefined` for a value that is never absent.

10. **The plugin's withheld log line** branches on `w.source`: the host-configuration line names the option and its remedy; `error` for forbidden, `warn` otherwise — the existing level policy. RIGHT.

11. **Reach.** The option is reachable only by a host that constructs `SecurityPlugin` itself (cloud's control plane, embeddings). The CLI host (`serve.ts`, `schema-migration-plugins.ts`) constructs from `appSecurityPluginOptions(config)`, which returns `{ fallbackPermissionSet }` or nothing; there is no `objectstack.config.ts` key, so nothing an author writes is silently inert. RIGHT for this card (cloud adopts at a later pin); a CLI-hosted walled deployment cannot declare it until that host passes it through — a follow-up, not a defect of this diff.

12. **The card's prohibitions.** No NULL-`organization_id` row (the declared path writes nothing; the undeclared path is unchanged), no new table, no `packages/spec` file, `builtin-positions.ts` untouched. RIGHT.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23385-walled-accepted-defaults.md`: `'@objectstack/plugin-security': minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. It matches what the diff publishes — one new optional option, one new exported type, three trailing optional parameters, one optional `SuggestionDeps` member, one required field on an output-only type; nothing removed, renamed or narrowed in the accept set, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed. Each claim in its body (what was wrong, what is new, refused loudly, the exported widening) is true of the diff. Check Changeset on this head: success. RIGHT: `minor`.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (os-dev-report 6214518188):
- `src/index.ts` and the new boot test beyond the claim's file list — both inside the claimed package, and `index.ts` is required by the exported type. Accepted.
- The shared primary checkout detached and re-checked, and `git fetch --unshallow` on the shared `.git` — process notes with no effect on the diff; the seat should know the shared clone is now unshallow.
- PR #23883's body names this PR by branch, not by number — the seat may add the cross-link; both bodies state the landing order (this PR first, or together), which is right because #23883's line names an option `main` lacks until this lands.
- No pre-PR merge of a fresh `origin/main` — accepted: `main` is eight commits ahead of the base and none touches the reviewed surfaces (see Inputs); the queue rebuilds on current `main`.

Open questions, each answered:
1. Declared ⇒ sole source whatever the organization count — A, agreed. Under a wall D5 and section 1.5 put deployment standing in configuration; two sources would need a merge rule nothing governs; "declared means enforced" leaves no posture-by-count matrix; the undeclared host is unchanged. The one consequence (rows an organization accepted earlier are reported once as not read, naming the option) is pinned.
2. The list door refusing with 409 when declared — A, agreed. An empty list would hide the declared `isDefault` sets and show prompts no door can act on; the refusal names the option.
3. `WithheldAcceptance.source` required — A, confirmed (item 9 above).
4. Where PR #23883's line sits — answered on that PR's record.
5. The posture reading — A, agreed: the plugin's resolved `tenancyPosture` through `postureEnforcesWall`; a second `resolveTenancyPosture()` call would be the second reading the card forbids.

Out-of-scope observation (one organization and no `default` slug under a wall): an observation with no failing public door; it stays unfiled under Prime Directive #10. Agreed.

Added by this review:
- ADR-0090 D5 and its Alternatives 3 rejected an environment-level `defaultPermissionSets` setting as a second distribution channel outside the position system. This option is not that: the grant still flows through the `everyone` position's derived definition, so the explain path and the position audit see it; what the ruling moves under a wall is where the acceptance is recorded (configuration instead of a `resolved_by` row). Not a contradiction. PR #23883's line could name that rejected alternative to pre-empt the reading — optional.
- The sync's early return skips `collectDeclaredSuggestions` on a declared wall, so its once-per-engine report of a package whose manifest carries `permissions` in the ADR-0025 reading does not run there; a host that names such a set still sees it withheld as unserved. A diagnostic loss only; worth carrying into the follow-up that passes the option through the CLI host, if one is filed.
- The `Served-tier:` token: the dispatch asked for a contract-tier read of both PRs; the face rule (`reviewFace` over this PR's file list: the declaration face, no published schema and no governed path) fixes the token to `TIER_DEFAULT`, exact and not a floor, so that is what this record carries. The reading covered every file on the `Scope:` line.
- Check-runs on this head: all 40 completed; every gate-carrying job is `success` (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core 1 to 6 and the aggregate, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, both single-writer guards, the Part-of and claim guards, Check Documentation Links); the skips (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shards and Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance) are the expected-skips roster's PR-run skips. No local run.
- Landing: not a governed PR; it lands by the owning seat through the queue once ready, with this record as its `Clause-②: yes` review of record. The `needs:contract-review` label is not on the PR, so nothing is removed. The card stays open until #23883 lands (`Part of #23385`).
